primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - **PScore:** per-role XGBoost (2,000 rounds, lr 0.01, monotonicity constraints — only worthless-death and contest-loserate forced negative), standardized inputs, 5-fold CV.

primitives.assumptions: Skill follows Gaussian distribution; rating reflects confidence-adjusted mean.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in disentangling performance (PScore) from skill (OpenSkill rating) through role-aware modeling and Bayesian inference. PScore uses XGBoost to map 16 end-game features into a normalized percentile score, ensuring comparability across roles. This score is then used to update player skill via FFA OpenSkill, which assumes that individual performance rankings reflect underlying ability. The dual-rating system introduces a context-specific component (μ_i^ctx, σ_ctx^2) and a shared meta component (μ_i^meta, σ_meta^2), allowing skill to evolve differently within and across regions. Intra-region games update only the context component, while inter-region games update the meta component, enabling robust cross-pool comparisons. The system's failure mode occurs when isolated pools lack sufficient inter-context games, leading to poor meta calibration. Additionally, FFA updates reduce team-outcome forecasting accuracy but improve expert agreement and role fairness. The mathematical structure supports both probabilistic inference (GSI) and dynamic state transitions (GSE), with PScore acting as a derived kernel and OpenSkill as an isomorphic Bayesian operator.
